title: performance(canary): auto-detect perf regressions and add rollout guards
author: Priya Shah
description: Add automated detection of latency and throughput regressions for the performance canary pipeline and gate rollouts when regressions are detected. Motivation: we observed a few recent incidents where new model variants and runtime scheduler changes caused subtle 95th-percentile latency regressions that escaped manual review. This PR introduces a statistical regression detector that compares canary runs against a rolling baseline, integrates the detector into the canary runner, and wires up automatic rollout guards (fail-canary / pause-rollout) in the deployment orchestration. Work included: 1) a detector module implementing robust A/B comparison with configurable thresholds (absolute and relative), multiple metrics (p95 latency, p50/p90, qps, tail error-rate), and bootstrapped significance checks; 2) integration into the existing perf-canary runner so a failed detection marks the canary as failed and prevents automatic promote; 3) updates to CI perf workflows to run the detector as part of nightly canary runs; 4) Prometheus alert + Grafana dashboard changes to surface regression signals and suggested triage steps; 5) docs and runbook updates for oncall. This description is a continuous string and includes testing and rollout notes below. Testing: unit tests cover detector logic edge cases (small sample sizes, missing metrics), e2e harness runs against synthetic baseline and canary profiles, and a manual shadow rollout validated gating behavior. Backwards compatibility: default detector config mirrors previous manual thresholds so existing canaries behave identically unless teams opt-in to tighter sensitivity. Related Linear: ENG-4321, ENG-4479.
commits_summary: 4 commits: initial detector implementation; integrate detector with perf-canary runner; add CI workflow and dashboard config; docs and runbook updates.
ci_checks: lint: fail (flake8 on perf-canary/detector.py) - fixed in second commit
review_comments: Diego Ramos: Important change - can we make the detector config per-team? We should avoid global sensitivity. Requested change: add explicit override and documented default.
Priya Shah: Added per-team override and commented defaults in detector.py. Also added tests for custom thresholds.
Ava Martin: Minor: suggest clearer log lines when canary fails (include metric, delta, p-value). Changed accordingly.
Samir Patel: Approve after CI is green. Verified dashboard looks sane and alert thresholds match the detector outputs.
release_notes: Adds automated regression detection for perf canaries and rollout guards. By default behavior is compatible with existing thresholds; teams can configure sensitivity per-canary. Enables faster automatic gating of bad model/runtime changes.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for detector edge cases; integration test runs in CI against synthetic baselines; manual shadow rollout validating gating; added runbook steps for triage and rollback.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: false positives could block rollouts. Mitigation: conservative defaults, per-team sensitivity, manual override to force promote, and actionable runbook for triage. Added telemetry to measure detector false-positive rate.
notes_for_oncall: If a canary is failed by the detector, check observability-pack/canary_regressions dashboard for metric deltas and the detector p-value. If false positive, use the canary control plane to mark known-good baseline and re-run; escalate with ENG-4321 if detector behavior is unexpected.
human_readable_summary: This PR implements an automated statistical regression detector for performance canaries and wires it into the canary runner to prevent automatic promotions when regressions are detected. It includes tests, CI changes, dashboard/alert updates, and documentation.
internal_references: See ENG-4321 for product-level goals and ENG-4479 for dashboard/alerting work. Related perf canary PRs: pr-2143-performance-canary-auto-detection-rollout-guards.json, pr-9812-performance-canary-rollout-guards.json.
changelog_entry: perf(canary): auto-detect regressions and gate rollouts (ENG-4321)
context_and_motivation: Recent incidents showed that subtle latency regressions were catching teams by surprise. Automating detection reduces MTTR and prevents bad variants from promoting to production. This PR is the first step towards continuous, automated regression monitoring in our canary pipeline.
follow_up_work: 1) Add model-variant-aware baselines to reduce noise; 2) add adaptive sensitivity based on traffic volume; 3) surface per-pr summaries in GitHub status for quick developer feedback (ENG-4520).
